sections.h2: Selling a house in Riviera Beach
sections.html:
Waterfront living defines Riviera Beach, a compact Palm Beach County city of about 39,357 people as of July 2025. The Port of Palm Beach lies inside its limits, and the city covers both the mainland and part of Singer Island. A seller typically picks from three routes.

  • Hire an agent and wait for a conventional buyer.
  • Sell directly to a buyer you find yourself.
  • Accept a cash purchase of the house as it stands, on your schedule.

Lots, ages and styles are mixed, so the condition of the house and its exact location drive the price more than any citywide number.

Renters make up a large share of this dense city: owners live in 62.2 percent of homes, so nearly two in five households rent. Plenty of houses sell with tenants in place, which makes lease and deposit records worth having on hand.

sections.h2: Palm Beach County homestead rules for sellers
sections.html:
A homestead takes $25,000 off the first $50,000 of assessed value for all taxes. A second exemption applies to everything except school taxes, with a 2025 maximum of $25,722. You qualify based on January 1 status and must apply by March 1.

Qualifying exemptions renew automatically, and a receipt card goes out on the last business day of December. Tell the property appraiser by phone or email if ownership changes through sale, marriage, divorce or death, or if the use changes. Because a homestead stays with the owner, a buyer files a new application.

Under Save Our Homes, yearly assessed-value growth is limited to 3 percent or the CPI change, whichever is lower, and a sale resets the property to just value. With Amendment 3 approved on November 3, 2026, the Palm Beach office can explain how the larger exemption works from 2027.

Filing options are the online E File system, five service centers or a mailed form, and ownership-change calls go to 561.355.2866. Bring Social Security numbers for all owners and spouses, a Florida driver's license and a second proof of residence, such as voter registration or a utility bill for the property.

  • Report a move-out so the exemption ends cleanly.
  • Ask about portability if you are buying another Florida homestead.

Delinquency starts April 1, and the county tax collector sells tax certificates on unpaid items by June 1. Whoever accepts the lowest interest rate wins the certificate, with bids in quarter-percent steps (section 197.432).

Two years after April 1 of the issuance year, a certificate holder may apply for a tax deed, with a $75 application fee under section 197.502. On a homestead, the opening bid adds one-half of the latest assessed value to the amounts due. The clerk holds a public auction, and the high bidder posts the larger of 5 percent or $200 and pays the balance within 24 hours, not counting weekends and holidays.

If a certificate sits on your house, selling before the deed process can protect the equity you have left. The Palm Beach tax collector can give you the redemption total, which you should not estimate.

Because about two in five households rent, many houses here sell with tenants. A month-to-month tenancy ends only with at least 30 days' notice before the end of a monthly period, and after a court judgment the sheriff acts on the writ following 24 hours' posted notice (sections 83.57 and 83.62).

Outside Miami-Dade, the clerk collects 70 cents of stamp tax per $100 when the deed is recorded, and every signer is liable. Recording itself costs $5.00 for page one and $4.00 for each added page under section 28.24, plus technology charges.

  • Ask the closing agent for lien payoffs and a tax proration.
  • Gather leases and deposit records for the buyer.
  • Line up the two witnesses the deed needs.

sections.h2: Selling with tenants in the house
sections.html:
A sale does not end a lease. The buyer takes the house subject to it, so a tenant with time left stays unless a lawful notice or agreement ends the tenancy. Tell the tenant in writing that a sale is coming, and keep showings to reasonable hours and with notice.

If the buyer wants the house empty, ask early. A cash buyer may wait until the lease ends, or may offer to pay for a move-out, and either deal belongs in the contract. If the tenant owes rent, your title agent can show how it is handled at closing. Hand over the lease, the deposit amount and any management agreement so the buyer is not surprised.

Check the rent roll against the lease before you sign anything. A cash buyer will price in a below-market rent, while a retail buyer who plans to live in the house may ask you to deliver it vacant.

sections.h2: Does living near the port or Singer Island change how a house is marketed?
sections.html:
It does. The port is part of the waterfront identity, and the waterfront marketplace draws visitors headed for the cruise ships. Houses near the water or the marinas are judged on views, boat access and insurance costs. Inland houses are judged on lot size, roof age and distance to the bridges.

Pull your flood zone information, insurance policy and permit records together before you talk price, so a buyer can weigh ongoing costs as well as the sale price. Sellers who document these early usually face fewer renegotiation requests after inspection.

1. Give the buyer the address, your mortgage balance and who lives in the house.
  2. Study the written offer for price, repair terms and closing day.
  3. The title agent searches the record and orders payoff letters.
  4. Sign the deed with two witnesses watching.
  5. The clerk records it, then your proceeds are released.

Before the first call, collect your payoff letter, newest tax bill, any lease and your insurance declarations page. Ask every buyer how long the offer lasts, who pays for the title policy and whether the price can change after an inspection, and get the answers in writing.

With cash, no lender appraisal stands in the way, so title work sets the pace. Keep copies of the signed settlement statement and the recorded deed.

faqs.q: Is a tenant-occupied Riviera Beach house sellable?
faqs.a: Yes. A lease generally continues until its term or a proper notice ends it, so give the buyer's title agent the lease, deposit records and any management agreement.

faqs.q: Does the buyer keep my Palm Beach homestead exemption?
faqs.a: No. A homestead does not pass to a buyer, and you should report the sale to the property appraiser.

faqs.q: What is the stamp tax rate on a Riviera Beach deed?
faqs.a: Seventy cents per $100 of consideration, as in every county except Miami-Dade. All parties to the document are liable.

faqs.q: When do unpaid property taxes become delinquent?
faqs.a: April 1, with certificates sold on unpaid items by June 1.

faqs.q: Is a cash sale quicker than listing here?
faqs.a: Often, since no lender appraisal is needed. The title must still be clear, and the deed witnessed and recorded before closing.
